content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no non-compete or field-of-use restriction binding us as Licensee.

What I checked and why it does not trigger the rule:

- **Art. X (Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation)** — the natural home for a covenant like this contains only nondisclosure (p0124) and a non-solicitation of Licensor's employees (p0125). No restraint on our competing activities.
- **"FIELD OF USE" definition (p0007) and Art. II Additional Restrictions (p0027, p0040–p0047)** — these limit how we may use *Licensor's* Licensed Technology (Spot FX data/order transmission only; no sublicensing, distribution, reverse engineering, or Derivative Works of the Licensed Technology). That is ordinary license-scope drafting, not a field-of-use restriction on our business: nothing stops us from licensing another platform, running other business lines, or building our own technology independently.
- **Change of Control (p0134)** — Licensor is deemed to withhold consent reasonably if an acquirer competes with it. This is a consent/termination right, not a covenant restricting what we may do, so it belongs to the change-of-control/assignment rule rather than NONCOMPETE (worth a separate look under that rule, along with the Art. XXII right of first refusal).

No redline proposed, consistent with the instruction not to flag license-scope or Vendor-side restrictions.
